Exact-fingerprint Reference Sync review only: storefront browse/access checks whether the signed-in user is a platform or merchant actor to decide preview/storefront visibility. It does not authorize workforce admin operations, does not evaluate MFA readiness, and is not a semantic consumer of the server-side workforce AAL2 enforcement contract. The file remains unchanged to avoid turning storefront access into a second workforce auth authority.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This transaction changes privileged authorization semantics. A false PASS could allow an AAL1 workforce session to execute owner/admin, refund, integration/API or security-sensitive operations, while an over-broad rule could incorrectly force MFA on low-risk staff or customer accounts.

acceptanceCriteria: Platform owner requires AAL2 plus two verified TOTP factors before server-side admin authorization succeeds.
Platform admin and merchant owner/admin require current AAL2 plus at least one verified TOTP factor before server-side admin authorization succeeds.
A store role whose assigned permissions cross a sensitive boundary is elevated by the canonical policy; order-management refund authority is not silently treated as low-risk.

store.manage, integrations.manage and orders.manage authorization checks carry a canonical sensitive-boundary classification so direct API/Server Action calls cannot bypass step-up by skipping an admin page.
Low-risk support, analyst, viewer, catalog and marketing access remains AAL1-capable unless an explicit sensitive boundary is requested.
When required assurance is missing, page authorization redirects into the verified workforce MFA flow; authorization never falls back to a client flag or browser storage.
The workforce MFA context accepts only canonical sensitive-boundary values and can elevate, never lower, the role-derived requirement.
MFA provider/snapshot failures fail closed whenever AAL2 is required.
Customer login and customer MFA remain unchanged.
Middleware remains a coarse authentication/RBAC prefilter and is not promoted into a parallel MFA policy or factor authority.
invariants: Supabase Auth remains the sole MFA factor and AAL authority.
requiredWorkforceTotpFactors remains the canonical factor-count policy.
workforceAssuranceSatisfied remains the canonical server assurance predicate.
An unavailable MFA snapshot cannot satisfy a positive factor requirement.
A requested sensitive boundary may only increase assurance requirements.
No localStorage/sessionStorage/cookie flag represents MFA readiness.
Platform operator is not globally MFA-mandatory solely because it is a platform role; explicit sensitive authorization may still require step-up.

failureModes: requireAdmin authorizes a role before checking its required AAL2/factor count.
getAdminRequestUser protects UI navigation but a direct API request bypasses assurance.
A low-risk role is globally forced into MFA despite no sensitive authority.
An order manager can call the refund endpoint at AAL1 because orders.manage is treated as ordinary permission.
An integration or provider-management operation can run at AAL1 because integrations.manage/store.manage is not classified sensitive.
A platform operator is accidentally made globally MFA-required even for non-sensitive operations.
A caller supplies boundary=none to weaken a stronger role-derived requirement.
Supabase MFA list/AAL errors are interpreted as zero required factors rather than unavailable evidence.
AAL2 authorization logic is duplicated in middleware and diverges from server auth policy.
edgeCases: Platform owner with AAL2 and one verified TOTP factor remains blocked until two verified factors exist.
Platform admin with one verified factor at AAL1 is redirected to challenge, not authorized.
Merchant owner/admin with verified factor but AAL1 is redirected to challenge.
Order manager with AAL1 is elevated because refund authority crosses the sensitive boundary.
Support/viewer at AAL1 remains authorized for ordinary low-risk access.
Platform operator at AAL1 remains authorized for ordinary platform access but fails an explicit integration-api/security boundary.
An explicit boundary on the workforce login/context route cannot downgrade owner/admin or role-derived requirements.
MFA snapshot failure blocks required-assurance authorization while zero-factor low-risk access can continue.

alternatives.summary: Enforce AAL2 in requireAdmin/admin-api using the canonical policy and Supabase server assurance snapshot; middleware remains coarse prefilter.
alternatives.reason: It places proof at the actual server authorization boundary for pages, actions and APIs and avoids duplicating role/factor logic in edge middleware.

alternatives.summary: Re-resolve workforce roles and Supabase factors inside middleware and make it the primary AAL2 gate.
alternatives.reason: It would create a second policy/role-resolution path, risk drift from admin-api/requireAdmin and contradict the existing Identity authority boundary.

alternatives.summary: Require AAL2 for every workforce role regardless of permission.
alternatives.reason: The canonical roadmap explicitly preserves AAL1 for low-risk store workers unless their assigned authority crosses a sensitive boundary.

specialistReviews.finding: Returning null from an API authorization helper is only safe if the assurance decision happens before the actor is returned and direct requests cannot skip it.
specialistReviews.resolution: getAdminRequestUser and getPlatformRequestUser will incorporate server assurance before returning a user; callers cannot obtain an actor first and check MFA later.

specialistReviews.finding: Middleware should not become a second MFA/role authority.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep middleware read-only for this transaction; requireAdmin and admin-api remain the canonical authorization enforcement surfaces.

specialistReviews.finding: The accepted Market Ready workforce policy must preserve AAL1 for genuinely low-risk staff while requiring AAL2 for roles or permissions that cross refund, integration/API, permission, provider-credential or security boundaries.
specialistReviews.resolution: Derive sensitive assurance from canonical store roles/permission classifications and allow explicit boundary elevation without downgrade.

challenge.scenario: Platform owner has current AAL2 but only one verified TOTP factor.
challenge.finding: Checking only currentLevel would incorrectly authorize the owner.
challenge.resolution: Authorization uses workforceAssuranceSatisfied with the canonical required factor count of two.

challenge.scenario: Order manager enters the general admin at AAL1, then calls refund directly.
challenge.finding: Page-only enforcement would miss the sensitive API boundary.
challenge.resolution: Role-derived refund authority elevates the general workforce context and orders.manage is also classified as refund-sensitive inside admin-api.

challenge.scenario: Support or viewer enters admin at AAL1.
challenge.finding: A blanket workforce MFA rule would violate the roadmap.
challenge.resolution: No factor is required unless role or requested permission/boundary is sensitive.

challenge.scenario: MFA provider returns an error while an owner/admin request is being authorized.
challenge.finding: Falling back to the existing RBAC result would downgrade an availability failure into an auth bypass.
challenge.resolution: Positive assurance requirements use fail-closed snapshot semantics and no user is returned.

challenge.scenario: A client asks workforce-context for boundary=none after the server derived a stronger boundary from role authority.
challenge.finding: Client input could otherwise lower the requirement.
challenge.resolution: The server combines requested and role-derived boundaries monotonically; none never overrides a stronger boundary.

challenge.scenario: Middleware and requireAdmin independently implement role/factor policy.
challenge.finding: Two authorities can disagree and create bypasses or loops.
challenge.resolution: Middleware remains coarse prefilter; canonical AAL2 authorization lives only in server auth modules.

challenge.scenario: Reference Sync reports many unrelated consumers because generic implementation expressions such as export async function GET(){, auth.getUser(), if(!user)return null and catch{return null} also appear throughout the repository.
challenge.finding: Blindly editing those files would expand a high-risk identity transaction across unrelated customer, template, office and platform surfaces even though Implementation Sync reports no missing required consumer.
challenge.resolution: Acknowledge only the 45 exact finding fingerprints emitted by this head. No wildcard or rule-wide exception is used, and the unrelated files remain unchanged.

challenge.scenario: Full quality verification exposes legacy auth contracts and Sentinel overclaim after the first enforcement implementation.
challenge.finding: The first implementation replaced canonical hasStorePermission evaluation with the static role matrix, changed established fail-closed/rate-limit contract shapes, and claimed proof strength/dimensions beyond the current Guard Registry.
challenge.resolution: Restore hasStorePermission as the tenant permission authority, retain the established platform-role and fail-closed/rate-limit contracts, and reduce Completion Truth scope to strength 2 with only dimensions actually proven by Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build.

challenge.scenario: Reference Sync finds src/lib/storefront/access.ts because it uses the same platform_operators query expression as admin-api.
challenge.finding: The storefront module only determines browse/preview visibility and does not return an admin actor or authorize privileged workforce operations; wiring MFA enforcement into it would create cross-surface auth coupling.
challenge.resolution: Keep storefront access unchanged and acknowledge only the exact Reference Sync fingerprint for this consumer.

proofPlan: Add deterministic regression coverage for platform owner two-factor enforcement, platform/merchant admin AAL2 enforcement, low-risk AAL1 preservation and sensitive-permission elevation.
Prove direct admin-api authorization cannot return an actor before assurance is satisfied.
Prove requireAdmin redirects insufficient assurance to the verified workforce MFA flow and does not use browser-persisted readiness.
Prove workforce-context/login boundary input is canonicalized and cannot lower a stronger requirement.
Run full quality tests, TypeScript and production build.
Require exact-head Completion Truth and Lifecycle Closure before calling the block complete.

requirements.requirement: Canonical workforce role and sensitive-permission assurance is enforced at server-side admin authorization boundaries using Supabase AAL/TOTP evidence, while low-risk staff and customer auth remain unaffected.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Owner/admin or sensitive-permission requests must never receive an authorized actor at insufficient assurance.
Low-risk workforce roles remain AAL1-capable when no sensitive authority applies.
Customer login and customer MFA policy remain unchanged.
Middleware, browser state and custom OTP code do not become MFA authorities.

notes: Stage 1 MR1-WORKFORCE-IDENTITY high-risk enforcement block. Builds on merged PR #848 primitives and merged PR #849 workforce MFA UX. Middleware remains read-only as a coarse prefilter; AAL2 truth is enforced in canonical server auth boundaries to avoid split-brain policy. CI attempt 1 stopped at Plan Before Code because a non-canonical specialist role label was used; the review was relabeled to the canonical Operations role with no implementation change. Edit-Time Guard attempt 2 produced 45 SQ-KF-022 Reference Sync reviews from generic implementation-expression matches while Implementation Sync remained PASS with zero missing required consumers. Each review is acknowledged by exact file+fingerprint only; no broad exception was introduced. Full quality attempt 3 found four auth-contract regressions plus Sentinel proof overclaim. The remediation restores canonical hasStorePermission/legacy security contracts and narrows the completion claim from strength 3 + adversarial to the registry-supported strength 2 + tests/types/build/forbidden-state; no global guard semantics are changed.
